item.title: Trump offers UFC chief Dana White job of White House press secretary
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-08
WASHINGTON -- US President Donald Trump said Saturday he had offered Dana White, president and CEO of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC), the position of White House press secretary. In a post on Truth Social, Trump said he had asked White to bring assistants with him and named several UFC fighters. "I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States," Trump wrote. "I have requested that he bring with him assistants, even though some are not from our Country." "We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left. Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job!" Trump added. Shortly after Trump's announcement, White posted an image on Instagram showing himself standing behind the White House press briefing podium, accompanied by the caption "On to the next chapter," potentially signaling his willingness to accept the offer.

item.title: Chinese motorcycle brands turn heads at EICMA
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-08
MILAN, Italy -- A steady stream of visitors gathered around the booths of Chinese motorcycle makers at the 83rd International Two-Wheeler Exhibition (EICMA 2026) in Milan, Italy. Cameras were pointed at newly unveiled models, visitors paused to examine their designs and technical specifications, and conversations continued in the business areas behind the display, where overseas dealers explored potential deals and delivery arrangements. The scene offered a glimpse of how China's motorcycle industry is gaining visibility in Europe. EICMA, one of the world's major events for the motorcycle industry, was recently opened in Milan, bringing together various Chinese manufacturers. From traditional fuel-powered motorcycles to electric and smart mobility products, Chinese brands presented their latest models and technological advances.

item.title: Crested ibis-themed pavilion debuts at 9th CIIE
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-08
The Shared Beauty of the Crested Ibis Pavilion opened at the ninth China International Import Expo in Shanghai on Nov 6, bringing together 27 companies from China and five other countries for an exhibition featuring conservation projects, artwork, and products inspired by the bird. Jointly launched by the Shanghai People's Association for Friendship with Foreign Countries and the municipal government of Hanzhong, Shaanxi province, the pavilion gives Chinese and international participants a place to share their work and explore new ways to cooperate. At the opening ceremony, participating companies presented new products. L'Oreal China and Czech crystal maker Eleonora Crystal 1834 introduced conservation and public welfare initiatives. The program highlighted Shanghai Dance Theatre's The Crested Ibis, which premiered in 2014 and has since toured overseas.

item.title: When CIIE turns into an incubator?
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-08
At the Innovation Incubation Zone of the 9th CIIE, young tech entrepreneurs from across the globe gather here, bringing their technologies to Shanghai while seeking partners to turn ideas into reality. item.title: Chinese VP meets Georgian president
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-08
TBILISI -- Chinese Vice-President Han Zheng met with Georgian President Mikheil Kavelashvili in Tbilisi on Friday. Han conveyed Chinese President Xi Jinping's warm greetings and best wishes to President Kavelashvili. He said Georgia is China's first strategic partner in Transcaucasia and also the first country in Eurasia to establish a free trade arrangement with China. Over the 34 years since the establishment of diplomatic ties, the two sides have been upholding the principles of mutual respect, mutual trust and win-win cooperation and promoted the sound and steady development of bilateral relations, Han said. In June this year, Xi and Kavelashvili jointly announced the elevation of China-Georgia relations to a comprehensive strategic partnership, opening a new chapter for the development of bilateral ties and injecting fresh impetus into cooperation across various fields, he said. China stands ready to strengthen communication and coordination with Georgia, jointly deliver on the important consensus reached by the two leaders, and advance the development of China-Georgia relations, Han added. Consolidating and advancing China-Georgia relations serves the fundamental interests and shared aspirations of the two peoples, he said, adding the two sides should continue to firmly support each other on issues bearing on each other's core interests. China applauds Georgia's positive response to the four global initiatives proposed by Xi, and is ready to work with Georgia to act on these initiatives, jointly uphold the international system with the United Nations at its core and the international order underpinned by international law, Han said. The two sides should better align their development strategies, take high-quality Belt and Road cooperation as the guide to promote mutually beneficial cooperation across various fields, actively carry out people-to-people and cultural exchanges, and steadily foster closer bonds between the two peoples, he said. Kavelashvili asked Han to convey his sincere greetings and best wishes to Xi. He said that as ancient civilizations with long histories, Georgia and China respect and trust each other, their cooperative bonds keep tightening, and people-to-people exchanges are growing ever more frequent. Georgia takes great pride in its cooperation with China, he added. The Georgian president said that Georgia, as one of the earliest countries to join the Belt and Road Initiative, stands ready to deepen cooperation with China in connectivity, infrastructure development, trade and economy, tourism, sports, education and other areas, so as to deliver more benefits to both countries and greater well-being to their peoples, and continuously advance the Georgia-China comprehensive strategic partnership.

item.title: A new chapter begins: Giant pandas return to Zoo Atlanta
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-08
Two giant pandas from China, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, made their public debut at Zoo Atlanta on Nov 6, ending a two-year absence of giant pandas from the city. Their arrival opens a new chapter in giant panda conservation, building on 25 years of collaboration between Zoo Atlanta and its Chinese partners. Visitors welcomed the pair, while zoo officials highlighted the role of pandas in promoting wildlife conservation and cultural exchange. (Reporter: May Zhou, Video: Chelsea Ge)

item.title: Outside military involvement brings chaos to the SCS
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-08
A former Sri Lankan naval chief on Friday called for regional solidarity to safeguard peace and stability in the South China Sea, warning that outside military involvement in regional affairs risks spiraling into further escalation. "Outside military involvement in a domestic or regional matter is likely to lead to further chaos, and all will suffer," said Jayanath Colombage, former Chief of the Sri Lanka Navy and former Ambassador of Sri Lanka to Indonesia, on the sidelines of the 7th Symposium on Global Maritime Cooperation and Ocean Governance in Sanya, Hainan province.

item.title: Dalian Yingbo beat Tianjin Jinmen Tiger to win CSL title after 21 yrs
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-08
Dalian Yingbo beat Tianjin Jinmen Tiger to win CSL title after 21 years By Li Yingxue | chinadaily.com.cn | Updated: 2026-11-08 19:11 Share - WeChat Dalian Yingbo beat Tianjin Jinmen Tiger 3-1 at home on Sunday to clinch the 2026 Chinese Super League title on the final day of the season at Suoyuwan Football Stadium in Dalian, Liaoning province. [Photo/Xinhua] Snow blanketed the pitch, while the stands glowed blue. Neither the heavy snowfall nor the pressure of a title decider could stop Dalian Yingbo from making history. Dalian Yingbo beat Tianjin Jinmen Tiger 3-1 at home on Sunday to clinch the 2026 Chinese Super League title on the final day of the season, in front of 62,619 spectators at Suoyuwan Football Stadium in Dalian, Liaoning province. The triumph marks the return of the Chinese top-flight title to Dalian for the first time since 2005, when Dalian Shide last won the championship.
